--- title: "[SmoothBasis]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-abc}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Abstract base class for all smooth basis types. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/smooths/base.py#L11-L205){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python SmoothBasis() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Every smooth term in a GAM — a thin plate spline, a cubic regression spline, a P-spline, a Gaussian process smooth, and so on — is represented internally as a linear basis expansion `f(x) = B(x) @ beta` together with a quadratic roughness penalty `beta.T @ S @ beta`. This class fixes the contract that every basis type must satisfy so that the fitting machinery (penalized least squares, smoothing-parameter selection, prediction) can treat all basis types uniformly. Concrete subclasses differ only in how `B` and `S` are constructed, not in how they are consumed. Subclasses must implement `fit()`, `basis_matrix()`, `penalty_matrix()`, `null_space_dimension()`, and the `n_basis` property. The typical workflow is:: basis = MyBasis(k=10) basis.fit(x_train) B_train = basis.basis_matrix(x_train) # (n_train, k) B_new = basis.basis_matrix(x_new) # (n_new, k) S = basis.penalty_matrix() # (k, k) ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} A penalized basis decomposes its `k` basis functions into an unpenalized *null space* of dimension `M` (typically low-order polynomials, for which the penalty contributes nothing — e.g. a straight line has zero roughness under a second-derivative penalty) and a penalized *range space* of dimension `k - M`. The total penalty for smoothing parameter `lambda` is $$ \lambda \, \boldsymbol{\beta}^\top \mathbf{S} \boldsymbol{\beta}, $$ where `S` is symmetric positive semi-definite with `null_space_dimension()` zero eigenvalues. Basis types built on this contract may additionally supply identifiability constraints (via `identifiability_constraints()`) when the raw basis is not full rank on its own — for example when several smooth terms share an intercept and must each be constrained to have mean zero over the training data. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Any concrete subclass follows this pattern: ::: {#24d505a5 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np from whittaker.smooths import TPRS rng = np.random.default_rng(0) x = rng.uniform(0, 1, 100) basis = TPRS(k=10).fit(x) B = basis.basis_matrix(x) S = basis.penalty_matrix() B.shape, S.shape ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ((100, 10), (10, 10)) ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
is_fitted `True` after `fit()` has been called.
n_basis Number of basis functions `k`.
### [is_fitted]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} `True` after `fit()` has been called. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [is_fitted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Used internally (via `_check_fitted()`) to guard methods such as `basis_matrix()` and `penalty_matrix()` that depend on state computed during `fit()` (e.g. knot locations or transformation matrices), raising a clear error instead of failing on missing attributes when called out of order. ::: ### [n_basis]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Number of basis functions `k`. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [n_basis]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} This is the number of columns returned by `basis_matrix()` and the size of the (square) `penalty_matrix()`. It is fixed at construction time (e.g. via a `k` argument) and does not change after `fit()` is called. ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
basis_matrix() Evaluate basis functions at `x`.
fit() Fit the basis to training data.
identifiability_constraints() Return a constraint matrix `C` such that `C @ beta = 0`, or `None`.
null_space_dimension() Return the dimension `M` of the penalty null space.
penalty_matrix() Return the `(k, k)` roughness penalty matrix `S`.
### [basis_matrix()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Evaluate basis functions at `x`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/smooths/base.py#L88-L103){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python basis_matrix(x) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Covariate values. Shape `(n,)` for univariate or `(n, d)` for multivariate. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Design matrix of shape `(n, k)` where `k = self.n_basis`. ::: ### [fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the basis to training data. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/smooths/base.py#L68-L86){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fit(x) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Stores any parameters required for later calls to `basis_matrix()` (e.g. knot locations, transformation matrices). ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Training covariates. Shape `(n,)` for univariate smooths or `(n, d)` for multivariate smooths. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [self]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns the instance to allow method chaining. ::: ### [identifiability_constraints()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return a constraint matrix `C` such that `C @ beta = 0`, or `None`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/smooths/base.py#L142-L159){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python identifiability_constraints() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Some bases are not identifiable on their own once combined with other terms in a model (for example, several smooths sharing an intercept), and must be constrained — typically to have mean zero over the training data — before fitting. Subclasses may override this method to supply such sum-to-zero or other linear identifiability constraints; the default implementation returns `None`, meaning no constraint is required. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Constraint matrix of shape `(n_constraints, k)`, or `None` if the basis needs no identifiability constraint. ::: ### [null_space_dimension()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return the dimension `M` of the penalty null space. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/smooths/base.py#L124-L140){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python null_space_dimension() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The null space is the subspace of basis coefficients for which the roughness penalty is exactly zero — typically the low-order polynomials (e.g. constants and straight lines under a second-derivative penalty). By convention the first `M` columns of the basis matrix span this null space, so `S[:M, :M]` and the corresponding rows/columns of `S` involving those columns vanish. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The null space dimension `M`, satisfying `0 <= M < k`. ::: ### [penalty_matrix()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return the `(k, k)` roughness penalty matrix `S`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/smooths/base.py#L105-L122){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python penalty_matrix() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `S` encodes the quadratic wiggliness penalty applied to the basis coefficients: the total penalty contribution for smoothing parameter `lambda` is `lambda * beta.T @ S @ beta`. `S` is always symmetric positive semi-definite, with `null_space_dimension()` zero eigenvalues corresponding to the unpenalized functions (e.g. low-order polynomials) that the basis can represent for free. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Symmetric positive semi-definite matrix of shape `(k, k)` where `k = self.n_basis`. :::
